newsitem.title: USA: Reader's Digest says hires search firm for CEO.
newsitem.headline: Reader's Digest says hires search firm for CEO.

text.p: Troubled publishing group Reader's Digest Association Inc said Friday it hired executive search firm Spencer Stuart to help find a new chief executive to replace CEO James Schadt, who resigned earlier this week.
A Reader's Digest spokeswoman declined further comment on the search. Spencer Stuart officials also declined to comment.
"It's at the startup stage," one official, who declined to be identified, said of the search.
The firm will meet with the board's search committee at Reader's Digest offices next week, and will present a preliminary list of potential candidates.
George Grune, who preceded Schadt and was considered a powerful presence at the company, has taken over as interim CEO.
"Mr. Grune is the CEO and chairman of the company, and is acting as a very capable leader, with lot of experience in leading this company for now," the company spokeswoman said.
Grune was not expected to meet with the search firm immediately, the sources said.

Grune, 68, is chairman of two private foundations -- the DeWitt Wallace Reader's Digest Fund and the Lila Wallace Reader's Digest Fund -- that together own about 72 percent of the voting stake in the company.
Reader's Digest reported Thursday that it lost nearly $23 million in the fourth quarter as it struggled to revamp its businesses.
The company said it expects to take unspecified charges in the first quarter of 1998 associated with realigning business processes and operations.
On Aug. 11, the company announced that Schadt, 59, had resigned as chairman and CEO.
